hypothesis: reth's own [profile.maxperf] (fat LTO + codegen-units=1) on top of the cursor reuse lets LLVM inline across the jsonrpsee -> EthApi -> provider -> libmdbx crate boundaries that dominate both phases (per-call provider/factory clones, txn_execute closures, cursor get_value). Expect a few percent, mostly on the light phase's per-call glue; the MDBX seek and keccak kernels are unchanged.
llm_commentary: Fat LTO + codegen-units=1 on top of the cursor-reuse commit (4be52a6eda) is within noise on x86: c8a 5.10→5.07s with overlapping run ranges (5.05-5.13 vs 5.05-5.09), c8i 6.79→6.73s (6.71-6.85 vs 6.72-6.74). Only Graviton moves clearly, c8g 8.31→8.11s (-2.4%, ranges disjoint), plausibly because cross-crate inlining removes more call/return and atomic overhead on the per-call jsonrpsee→EthApi→provider→libmdbx glue there. That matches the profile: the hot work is the MDBX B-tree seek, keccak and kernel futex/scheduler time, none of which whole-program inlining changes, so the remaining compiler levers (znver5 on c8a, PGO) are unlikely to beat a few percent either. The bigger wins are still algorithmic: the per-SLOAD cached_storage_settings RwLock and address keccak, the per-op txn mutex, and the light phase's spawn_blocking handoff.
